comments.problem: FIXED and verified. The transport is now the plugin-side consumer: _execute_via_plugin_bridge reads the peer's stdout line-by-line, classifies reverse requests via _is_reverse_request (method present, no 'ok') and only accepts a response when msg.id == req_id AND 'ok' is present (line 472); a reverse request is serviced in-process through the injectable plugin_side (line 467 -> _serve_reverse_request), and without plugin_side the peer receives a hard PLUGIN_SIDE_UNAVAILABLE error envelope which converts to an honest HOST_UNAVAILABLE (never a fabricated COMPLETED, never a misparsed raw reverse request). Reproduced directly: execute_coder_semantic without plugin_side -> HOST_UNAVAILABLE, host_error='plugin bridge failed: bridge error HANDLER_ERROR: PLUGIN_SIDE_UNAVAILABLE: no plugin-side consumer wired' (no 'bridge error ERROR: {...semantic.execute...}' misparse); with plugin_side -> COMPLETED. E2E test_production_wiring_no_plugin_side_fails_closed_not_misparsed and test_round_trip_via_plugin_bridge_completed both pass.

scope_in: Contract: schema-validity of results (SemanticExecutionResult/1.0, all 12 fields)
scope_out: Plugin (TS) side implementation and real model execution
Schemas JSON files content review (only result validity against them)

out_of_scope_gaps.finding: bridge_peer._reverse_echo_test (line 149) calls reverse_request('semantic.execute', {'value': ...}) — params shape inconsistent with the request-carrying forward path ({"request": ...}); diagnostic helper only, not covered by E2E.

The peer does not validate the incoming SemanticExecutionRequest/1.0 before forwarding (validation lives only on the transport side); a non-transport client of the peer could push invalid requests through.

E2E has no coverage for the HARNESS_TRANSPORT=cli explicit-CLI rejection path (REJECTED_BY_HOST with the explicit-cli diagnostic), nor for auto-resolution with an unavailable bridge (REJECTED_BY_HOST legacy-fallback diagnostic).
